rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grep for banned words (honest, delve, landscape as verb, importantly, crucial, substrate, leverage as verb, synergize, paradigm shift) returned zero matches in body region (lines 1-55).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban in any curriculum/training surface.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No instances of 'ritual' or 'ceremony' in body. 'exercise' is used correctly per rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No stale markers found. Body contains no 2026- dates, 'caught live', 'compounded', 'MOVED', or transition-verb language in rule bodies.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 voice quintet (Boris/Martin/Godin/Sutherland/Siilasmaa) is employed. Line 9 'the agent can reverse-engineer your team's rules' is direct and matter-of-fact (Boris), line 27 'the ones you reject sharpen the read' is logical reframe (Martin). Tone is peer-warm and factual throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule applies to rough-cut article drafts. This is an exercise, not an article. Body is polished curriculum prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No recognizable practitioner techniques paraphrased. No move belongs to named framework requiring credit (Pocock, Klaassen, Martin, StoryBrand, JTBD, Huryn).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Consistently uses second person 'you' (line 5 'you do', line 22 'your team', line 43 'you'd write'). No third-person 'the student' or teacher framing like 'the trainer shows' or 'before students start'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 35: 'Adding a connector is one command per tracker.' The term 'connector' appears in maintainer block (line 62: 'Connector install is named, not taught') as a term-of-art. Used in body without one-breath earning. Rule requires: 'One-breath primer tied to what student just did or about to do, then real word.' Line 35 states fact about connectors but doesn't define what they are.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add one-breath primer before use: 'A connector links Claude Code to your team's tracker (GitHub, Linear, Jira). Adding a connector is one command per tracker. [MCP and connectors](...) has setup for your tracker, and it pays back on every session after this one.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reassurance-wrapped statements. Lines do not contain 'no penalty', 'fine way to', 'it's OK if', 'not a downgrade', 'you are not on the hook for X', 'sometimes humans should', 'not a box-check'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reference artifact with 'Frame to land' section. No user-given frame verbatim to be captured.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No practitioner names appear in body. No credit obligation triggered.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No punchy slogan with overstated reach requiring carve-out. Line 9 'the agent can reverse-engineer your team's rules' is modest and factual, not punchy.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No value-prop defensive language: no 'not an aspirational X', 'not a vendor Y', 'this isn't marketing', 'the real practitioners', 'unlike consultancy decks', 'grounded in actual', 'not theoretical', 'from the person running it'. Body teaches the practice.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Term 'convention' introduced at line 22 with concrete examples (Status, labels, severity, component, owner, repro steps). Earned in one breath tied to what student just did (read a ticket). Appropriate for M1.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No body-prose forcing function trimmed to a fenced prompt. No dangling pronouns or bypass-the-agent punchlines result from trim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Block at lines 50-54 is acceptable (exercise leaves durable artifacts: bug rules and close-out note). But violates standard shape: (1) 4 sentences instead of 1–3; (2) 54 words vs ceiling 25–40; (3) sentence 'The loop that started with a failing test closed' (line 52) narrates arc-positioning, violates §16's move 3 rule (destination only, no narrative). Per standard shape: Move 1 (Count+noun), Move 2 (qualifier), Move 3 (destination), no arc narration.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut 'The loop that started with a failing test closed.' Retain: 'Two things came out of one ticket: a close-out note on the bug you shipped, and the conventions your team has been encoding in its fields all along. The field rules stay in the scrollback. The next exercise sweeps this whole session.' (3 sentences, ~40 words).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Verbs describing student-agent interaction are peer-flat or warmer: 'ask Claude', 'tell Claude', 'have the agent work out'. No combative verbs (bark, order, command, whip, force, drag, push around, boss, shout at, snap at, lecture, scold).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All headers literally true: 'Read the ticket for your bug' (you read), 'Read the conventions off the ticket' (you infer from data), 'Write the close-out and send it' (agent writes, you send), 'Double-check the voice' (you check register), 'Anything can be reverse-engineered' (move applies broadly), 'What happened' (recap of artifacts).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No empty negation, deictic drumroll, bold-label echo, or citation/appendix duplication. Prose carries substance throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 27 'propose five bug rules' mentions count. Count does not appear adjacent to list; follows prompt marker. No list immediately below count to create redundancy.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 9 'the agent can reverse-engineer your team's rules' is not a superlative slogan. Claim is modest and true without needing carve-out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file does not state claims that repeat across other files. No source-stamp coordination required within this single exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Single-file evaluation. No sweep across multiple files with rule-set drift.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise frames work as building capability, not fixing lack. Line 9 'the agent can reverse-engineer your team's rules' is aspirational and outcome-focused. No 'you already think', 'you're missing', or deficiency framing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 35: 'connector' used without one-breath earning. Line states fact ('is one command per tracker') without defining term. OOB without prior M1 introduction. Per rule: 'One-breath primer tied to what student just did or about to do, then real word.' Reference to 'MCP and connectors' names page, not concept.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Same fix as check_writing.md rule 8: add definition in one breath (e.g., 'A connector links Claude Code to your team's tracker').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No narrating student's past or present state.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 52 'The loop that started with a failing test closed' narrates what student just did (past state / past-arc completion). Rule bans re-narration of 'what student just did'. This sentence re-narrates the M1 arc, not describing outcome or artifact destination. Violates Sutherland-flip principle (flip OFF student/arc ONTO artifact).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete sentence. Use artifact-side framing for remaining block: 'Two things came out of one ticket: a close-out note on the bug you shipped, and the conventions your team has been encoding in its fields all along. The field rules stay in the scrollback. The next exercise sweeps this whole session.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No conflation of memory vs context. 'Field rules stay in the scrollback' (line 53) correctly describes scrollback as context, with next exercise compounding into memory.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 14-15 recovery path ('If there is no ticket for this bug, say so in the chat. The agent will offer to create one') passes base test: plausible (no ticket exists), non-obvious (agent creates one), time-critical window closes at session end. Must stay visible in body per boundary clause.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule about prompts specifying shape only when teaching depends on it. Exercise body doesn't over-specify prompt structure; prompts are simple.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No debrief or retro interview present in exercise body. Exercise is action-focused, not reflective closure.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No patterns from other modules (M2 planning, M4 testing, M5 long-running work). Voice is consistent with M1 ticket-reading exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 41-43 'Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?' is reading for emotional payoff (checking voice register), not error-catching. Rule explicitly allows: 'Reading for emotional payoff (feeling citations land, feeling output sound like company) stays.' Student steers agent if tone misses.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Simulation personas never alone.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No simulation personas (Teacher Claude, Builder Claude) in this exercise. Exercise is live session, not simulation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No callout boxes with research framing. No consultant-deck-style research box.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All student moves (lines 13-48) are within conversation with agent. No editor/terminal primitives forced. Recovery path (line 14-15) stays in chat ('say so in the chat'). All instructions route through agent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No mention of CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, or rules files in student-facing body. No layer specification required.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No em-dashes in body. Sentences are simple and direct throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers at imperative-action sections all use verbs: 'Read the ticket' (line 11), 'Read the conventions' (line 20), 'Write the close-out' (line 33), 'Double-check the voice' (line 41). Per rule: 'when student acts' → lead with verb. All correct.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 35 link: '[MCP and connectors](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md)' uses title 'MCP and connectors', not filename 'mcp-and-connectors.md'. Per rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives (memory, skill, rule, plan, agent, subagent). Exercise does not author these contested terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 9 'the agent can reverse-engineer' correctly uses 'agent' for acting/autonomous work. Line 27 'Ask Claude to reverse-engineer' correctly uses 'Claude' for addressee. Vocabulary discipline maintained.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Terminology correct: 'this session' (line 52), 'task' (closing a bug), no misuse of 'run' outside CI/eval context.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No time-of-day phrasing: no 'tomorrow', 'overnight', 'this morning', 'tonight', 'next morning', 'yesterday', 'last night'. Body is time-agnostic.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No contemplative-pause headers or sentence-form prefixes announcing reflection. No 'Pause', 'Meta-moment', 'Step back', 'Moment of truth', 'sit with', 'let it land', 'take a moment', 'give yourself space', 'breathe'. Actions carry reflection implicitly.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No meta-asks where student already decided. Prompts ask Claude to act after student provides input (line 13 'paste its link', line 27 asks for rules from ticket, line 37 asks for close-out). No 'ask me what you decided' redundancy.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No artifact save instruction in body prose (prompts will handle destination). Rule not fired on exercise body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Each sentence advances toward the work: opening frames the task, bullets describe steps, prompts ask for action. No implementation detail before point-of-use, no administrative aside, no extra source trivia.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 41-43 asks student to check voice of ticket comments (pre-session artifact), not bare 'read it' after Claude prints. Comparative judgment task, not patronizing re-narration of read action.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No forward-callout section or closer gesturing at what student will do/find/notice across rest of training.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Timing widget (line 3) is correctly placed at moment of use. No operational settings (thinking-effort level, model choice, mode tag) requiring per-module reminder.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body uses training's own earned concepts correctly: 'the loop' (line 52 — closing the loop that started with failing test). No invented synonyms or jargon not anchored in training theory.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 35 'Adding a connector' names action (artifact), not 'typing add' or 'saying add'. Line 37 'Ask Claude to write the close-out' — 'write the close-out' is artifact-noun phrasing, not 'type' or 'tell'. Correct throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No CLI recipes walked through step-by-step. Line 35 names state needed ('connector installed'), not mechanics ('run command, follow auth flow'). Exercise avoids talking down to engineers on standard setup.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 52 'The loop that started with a failing test closed' narrates arc-positioning (M1's narrative arc) rather than student outcome. Subject test: sentence is about training's arc, not student's artifact or outcome. Deletion test: neighbors read clearly without it. Per rule: arc-narration is highest-yield NVA in corpus.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete sentence. Result: 'Two things came out of one ticket: a close-out note on the bug you shipped, and the conventions your team has been encoding in its fields all along. The field rules stay in the scrollback. The next exercise sweeps this whole session.' (3 sentences, artifacts as subjects, destination clear.)
